title: A Linear issue comment claims an issue fixed that never actually closed
author: nisaba
description: The second recipe to read a toolkit besides github/x at all -- grepped every one of the 67 existing recipes' own recipe.json toolkit field before writing this one: the set is exactly {github, github+x, x+github, slack+github}, one non-github/x toolkit already live (slack+github, RECIPES/slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue/, the sixty-seventh real recipe), so this is the second cell in a growing family, not a repeat of the one exception. Extracts every real GitHub closing-keyword claim (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses, the shared seam_engine.closing_keywords grammar fourteen sibling recipes already import) from a Linear issue comment's own text and cross-checks it against the live issue tracker's own state -- the Linear-side twin of mention-claims-unfixed-issue (the X-mention leg) and slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue (the Slack-channel-message leg), same seam, a third inbound surface entirely: a comment left on a Linear issue, not a tweet, a mention, or a Slack channel message. An issue that exists but is still open is the seam: a comment sitting on a Linear issue already disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on either platform ever compares them. Proposed per CONTRIBUTING.md's own 'New toolkits' section, the exact same way gmail_calendar.py proposed gmail/google_calendar and slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue proposed slack/github before either had a live scope -- fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the comment's own created_at, holding mention-claims-unfixed-issue's/slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue's identical 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number for a second new toolkit. A claim checked within 24 hours of posting might still be a race (the real fix landing moments after the comment went out) rather than a settled public overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named issue still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-unfixed-issue sibling: the claimed issue's own live state field, verified against ListIssues, not a guess about which tracker the commenter meant. A named issue that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future Linear-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named issue that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A comment with no closing-keyword claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the Linear commenter -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
